references.text: Abram traveled through the land to the place of Shechem, to the oak of Moreh. At that time the Canaanites were in the land.
Shechem son of Hamor the Hivite, the ruler of the area, saw Dinah, took her, lay with her and humiliated her.
Jacob gave Joseph one portion more than his brothers, which he had taken from the Amorites with his sword and bow.
Joseph's bones, which the Israelites had brought up from Egypt, were buried in Shechem, on the plot of land that Jacob had bought from Hamor's sons for a hundred kesitahs.
All Job's brothers and sisters and all who knew him before came to him and gave each one a kesitah and a gold ring – one of only a few other places in the Bible where 'kesitah' is mentioned.
Stephen mentions that our ancestors were brought to Shechem and laid in the tomb that Abraham had bought from Hamor's sons in Shechem for a sum of money.
Direct narrative continuation: Hamor comes out to Jacob shortly after Jacob has bought the plot of land in Shechem.
Part of the same narrative: Hamor and his son react to Jacob's presence in what he had just purchased.
Direct narrative link: Shechem's request for Dinah occurs in the same context as Jacob's purchase of the plot of land.
